title: Burst orchestration policy for dedicated fleets and graceful overage handling
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Customers on Dedicated capacity occasionally exceed their committed throughput due to sudden traffic spikes. We currently provide temporary surge lanes but lack a standardized orchestration policy that balances latency SLOs, predictable billing, and operator visibility. This ticket defines a burst orchestration policy for Dedicated fleets that combines short-lived temporary boosts, phased surge pools, and an invoice smoothing model to avoid surprising charges while preserving service availability.

Goals:
- Define a policy for allocating temporary burst capacity (temporary boosts) to tenants on Dedicated pools with clear limits, timeboxes, and operator controls.
- Implement a phased surge-pool orchestration layer that can: 1) prefer tenant-reserved lanes, 2) spill into shared provisional pools, 3) apply backoff to non-critical workloads when capacity is constrained.
- Design and implement overage billing behavior that amortizes short bursts instead of immediate steep charges: a grace window, prorated smoothing, and clear invoice line items.
- Provide tenant-facing signals and operator tools: realtime burst metrics, projected invoice impact, and a manual override playbook for support.

Non-goals:
- This scope does not include wholesale pricing model changes for Dedicated contracts (that is a PM-commercial workstream).
- Not building a new hardware allocator; we will reuse the existing fleet allocator and extend policies on top.

Acceptance criteria:
- Traffic controller can allocate a temporary boost with duration cap (configurable, default 15 minutes) and per-tenant limit in QPS and burst tokens.
- Surge pool admission uses a 3-step decision: reserved lanes -> tenant soft-commit lanes -> provisional shared surge pool. Fallback policy enforced when pool usage > 85%.
- Billing pipeline receives per-tenant burst events and produces a smoothed invoice delta that applies a linear amortization over the subsequent invoice period when burst duration < grace window.
- Console shows a burst timeline, estimated cost delta, and a ‘pre-approve’ toggle for customers who opt into auto-burst billing.
- Operator runbook created with steps for manual reclamation, tenant communication templates, and escalation to infra team.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Timebox length: 15 minutes default chosen to capture typical user spikes (cron bursts, search indexing) while limiting long-running over-provisioning. Longer windows materially increase reserve costs.
- Meter granularity: switched from 1s to 60s for billing events to reduce aggregation noise and storage cost; this smooths short microbursts but preserves visibility for user-impacting spikes.
- Smoothing algorithm: linear amortization chosen over threshold-based discounts because it’s easier to explain on invoices and composes well with existing usage buckets. We may iterate to a hybrid model after customer feedback.
- Priority fencing: we avoid hard preemption of tenant traffic except for explicitly low-priority labels to reduce customer surprises. Instead we use graceful backpressure with token-bucket shaping where possible.

Implementation plan:
1) Controller extension: add 'burst_token' object and lifecycle to the fleet controller, with admin API for operator overrides (4d).
2) Surge pool manager: implement provisional pool admission flow and policy engine (6d).
3) Billing events: extend usage collector to emit 'burst_event' with duration, peak QPS, pool type, and amortization tag (4d).
4) Console changes: burst timeline widget, projected cost estimate, and pre-approve toggle (3d).
5) Runbook and dashboards: create Grafana panels (burst capacity, admission rate, queue times) and a playbook doc in Confluence (2d).
6) Staging load test and canary: run k6 scenarios, review latency & tail p99 under bursts, release gated by SLO checks (4d).

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New SLI: % of burst requests served within tenant SLO during a burst window (target 99% over 30d).
- Billing accuracy: mismatch between projected amortized cost and final invoice for bursts should be < 2% over 30 days.
- Alerting: surge pool saturation (>85%) triggers a P1 alert and creates a support ticket with affected tenants list.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag behind dedicated-burst-policy. Start with internal tenants and a small set of pilot customers.
- Phase 1: enable read-only signals and projected invoice estimations for 1 week.
- Phase 2: enable automatic provisional pool admission for pilot tenants and observe.
- Phase 3: enable billing amortization for pilot tenants and review finance reconciliation.

Open questions / decisions needed from PM/Finance:
- Grace window length for amortization (default 15 minutes proposed).
- Per-tenant burst quota: should this be percentile-based (e.g., 99th) or absolute static caps?
- Tenant opt-in model vs default opt-out for amortized billing.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEDICATED/Burst+Orchestration+Policy
- GitHub RFC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/282
- Mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/dedicated-burst-console
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Burst/tenant-burst-overview

Notes on backward compatibility:
- Existing Dedicated customers without the pre-approve toggle will continue to be charged using legacy per-token overage until migration finishes. The migration path and communications are handled by PM.

QA plan:
- Unit tests for admission logic and billing amortization math.
- Integration tests simulating concurrent tenant bursts and measuring admission fairness.
- End-to-end billing verification in a staging environment against synthetic invoices.

Expected risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Surprise charges for customers who misunderstand amortization. Mitigation: console projections + pre-approve opt-in + email notifications for first three bursts.
- Risk: Surge pool starvation for high-priority tenants. Mitigation: implement priority labels and emergency manual reclamation API.
- Risk: Incorrect billing math causing finance reconciliation drift. Mitigation: staging reconciliation run and weekly sampling for first month.

Next steps:
- PM to confirm grace window and opt-in policy (blocked until decision).
- Engineering to draft API schema and telemetry contract (in progress).
- Schedule design review with Console and Billing teams for 2026-03-05.
